children.text: In the two-slit electron interference experiment, a monochromatic point source \(S\) emits electrons through an electron biprism onto a screen. The biprism consists of a grounded cylindrical wire mesh with a thin central filament \(F\), directed into the figure. \(S_1,S_2\) are virtual sources separated by \(d\). The source-to-biprism distance is \(\ell\), and the biprism-to-screen distance is \(L\). The diagram is not to scale. Experiments were performed by Mollenstedt and colleagues, Merli, Missiroli and Pozzi, and Tonomura and colleagues.

nodes.alt: Original electron biprism ray diagram: source S and virtual sources S1 and S2 separated by d, filament F in grounded mesh, distances ell and L, screen, transverse x axis, propagation z axis, filament radius a and mesh radius b.

children.text: Take the filament cross-section centre as origin \(O\). Find the potential \(V(x,z)\) near the filament in terms of filament surface potential \(V_a\), filament radius \(a\), and mesh radius \(b\). Ignore mirror charges.

An incoming electron plane wave has wave-vector component \(k_z\). Find its induced transverse component \(k_x\) due to the biprism in terms of electron charge, \(v_z,V_a,k_z,a,b\), with \(|k_x|\ll k_z\). Use \(\mathbf k=2\pi\mathbf p/h\).
Before \(S\), electrons are accelerated from a field-emission tip through potential \(V_0\). Find the nonrelativistic wavelength using rest mass \(m\), charge and \(V_0\).

Use \(v_z=c/2\), \(V_a=10\,\mathrm V\), \(V_0=50\,\mathrm{kV}\), \(a=0.5\,\mu\mathrm m\), \(b=5\,\mathrm{mm}\), \(\ell=25\,\mathrm{cm}\), \(L=1.5\,\mathrm m\), \(h=6.6\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}\), electron charge magnitude \(e=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\), rest mass \(m=9.1\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), and \(c=3\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\).
Find the interference fringe spacing on the screen.
If the electron wave is spherical instead of planar, is its fringe spacing larger, equal or smaller than in d.ii?
Find the percentage wavelength error caused by using the nonrelativistic approximation in part c.
Find the separation \(d\) of the apparent double slits.

Conventions: use positive e for the electron-charge magnitude. The transverse deflection changes sign on opposite sides of the filament, so the automatic k_x fields ask for its magnitude. Retain the supplied v_z for deflection and V_0 for wavelengths, as the official calculation does.

Question 2: Electron biprism
In the two-slit electron interference experiment, a monochromatic point source \(S\) emits electrons through an electron biprism onto a screen. The biprism consists of a grounded cylindrical wire mesh with a thin central filament \(F\), directed into the figure. \(S_1,S_2\) are virtual sources separated by \(d\). The source-to-biprism distance is \(\ell\), and the biprism-to-screen distance is \(L\). The diagram is not to scale. Experiments were performed by Mollenstedt and colleagues, Merli, Missiroli and Pozzi, and Tonomura and colleagues.

a
Take the filament cross-section centre as origin \(O\). Find the potential \(V(x,z)\) near the filament in terms of filament surface potential \(V_a\), filament radius \(a\), and mesh radius \(b\). Ignore mirror charges.
b
An incoming electron plane wave has wave-vector component \(k_z\). Find its induced transverse component \(k_x\) due to the biprism in terms of electron charge, \(v_z,V_a,k_z,a,b\), with \(|k_x|\ll k_z\). Use \(\mathbf k=2\pi\mathbf p/h\).
c.i
Before \(S\), electrons are accelerated from a field-emission tip through potential \(V_0\). Find the nonrelativistic wavelength using rest mass \(m\), charge and \(V_0\).
c.ii
Find the wavelength including relativity.
Use \(v_z=c/2\), \(V_a=10\,\mathrm V\), \(V_0=50\,\mathrm{kV}\), \(a=0.5\,\mu\mathrm m\), \(b=5\,\mathrm{mm}\), \(\ell=25\,\mathrm{cm}\), \(L=1.5\,\mathrm m\), \(h=6.6\times10^{-34}\,\mathrm{J\,s}\), electron charge magnitude \(e=1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm C\), rest mass \(m=9.1\times10^{-31}\,\mathrm{kg}\), and \(c=3\times10^8\,\mathrm{m/s}\).

Calculate \(k_x\).
d.ii
Find the interference fringe spacing on the screen.
d.iii
If the electron wave is spherical instead of planar, is its fringe spacing larger, equal or smaller than in d.ii?
d.iv
Find the percentage wavelength error caused by using the nonrelativistic approximation in part c.
d.v
Find the separation \(d\) of the apparent double slits.

solution.text:
Question 2: Electron biprism
a. Cylindrical potential
For line charge density \(\lambda_q\), Gauss's law gives \(E_r=\lambda_q/(2\pi\epsilon_0r)\). Integrate with \(V(b)=0\) and eliminate \(\lambda_q\) using \(V(a)=V_a\):
\[V(r)=\frac{\lambda_q}{2\pi\epsilon_0}\ln\frac br=V_a\frac{\ln(b/r)}{\ln(b/a)},\qquad r=\sqrt{x^2+z^2}.\]
b. Transverse impulse
With electron charge \(-e\), the force is \(F_x=e\,\partial V/\partial x=-eV_ax/[(x^2+z^2)\ln(b/a)]\). To leading small-deflection order, treat \(x\) and \(v_z\) as constant during transit. The near-filament straight-line approximation extends the impulse integral to infinite limits:
\[\Delta p_x=\frac1{v_z}\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}F_x\,dz=-\operatorname{sgn}(x)\frac{\pi eV_a}{v_z\ln(b/a)}.\]
\[|k_x|=\frac{2\pi}{h}|\Delta p_x|=\frac{2\pi^2 eV_a}{hv_z\ln(b/a)}.\]
Equivalently, solve the transverse equation of motion for the small slope \(|dx/dz|=\pi eV_a/[mv_z^2\ln(b/a)]\) in a nonrelativistic trajectory treatment, then use \(k_x/k_z\simeq dx/dz\). In the relativistic form use \(p_z=\gamma mv_z\), so the same impulse-to-wave-vector result follows. The positive source result is the magnitude, although an intermediate impulse is evaluated at positive \(x\) with an inconsistent sign.
c. de Broglie wavelengths
Nonrelativistically, \(p^2/(2m)=eV_0\). Relativistically, total energy is \(mc^2+eV_0\), so \(p^2c^2=(mc^2+eV_0)^2-m^2c^4\). Hence
\[\lambda_\mathrm{nr}=\frac h{\sqrt{2meV_0}},\qquad \lambda_\mathrm{rel}=\frac h{\sqrt{2meV_0\left(1+\dfrac{eV_0}{2mc^2}\right)}}.\]
d. Numerical results and geometry
\[|k_x|\simeq3.46\times10^7\,\mathrm{m^{-1}}.\]
The two symmetric plane-wave components have transverse wave vectors \(+k_x\) and \(-k_x\), so their interference phase difference is \(2k_xx\). The fringe spacing is
\[s=\frac\pi{|k_x|}\simeq9.07\times10^{-8}\,\mathrm m=90.7\,\mathrm{nm}.\]
With a spherical incident wave, geometric divergence makes the fringe spacing larger than the plane-wave result. This qualitative comparison remains self-review.
\[\lambda_\mathrm{nr}\simeq5.47\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm m,\qquad\lambda_\mathrm{rel}\simeq5.34\times10^{-12}\,\mathrm m,\]
\[100\frac{\lambda_\mathrm{nr}-\lambda_\mathrm{rel}}{\lambda_\mathrm{rel}}\simeq2.4\%.\]
The official apparent-double-slit estimate inserts its d.ii fringe spacing and relativistic wavelength into \(s=\lambda_\mathrm{rel}(\ell+L)/d\), giving \(d\simeq1.03\times10^{-4}\,\mathrm m\). The response is for self-review because this substitution mixes two wavefront models. A consistent virtual-source construction must also change the fringe spacing.
Source-model caveat: the source mixes the plane-wave fringe spacing with the virtual-point-source formula in the last estimate. A self-consistent spherical-source geometry instead gives \(d=2\ell|k_x|/k_z\) and a larger spacing \(s=\pi(\ell+L)/(\ell|k_x|)\). Using the supplied relativistic wavelength gives \(d\simeq1.47\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm m\).
